findings.title: search.init goroutine panics when the events channel is closed
findings.body: In the goroutine started by search.init, the receive `v := <-events` is not in the comma-ok form, and the loop then unconditionally calls `s.handleEvent(watchctx, v)`. The SQL backend closes the events channel via `defer close(stream)` when its poller returns (e.g., when backend.Stop calls cancel and `b.done` closes). After that, every iteration of the for loop receives nil for `v` (zero value of *WrittenEvent), and `s.handleEvent(watchctx, nil)` then dereferences `evt.Type` on a nil receiver, panicking the goroutine. Because the search watch is now started eagerly inside NewResourceServer on every startup, the lifecycle that closes this channel is reached on every shutdown. The receive should be `v, ok := <-events` with `if !ok { return }` so the goroutine terminates cleanly when the backend is torn down.

findings.title: Finer-grain cache lock lets two callers build the same index concurrently
findings.body: After this PR, bleveBackend.BuildIndex only takes cacheMu around the final map assignment (`b.cache[key] = idx`); the actual index creation (bleve.New/bleve.NewMemOnly and the ListIterator walk) runs unlocked. getOrCreateIndex itself has no synchronization, so two concurrent callers with the same NamespacedResource can both observe an empty cache (GetIndex returns nil), both call s.build, each constructs its own bleveIndex (running through the storage ListIterator independently), and then both contend on b.cacheMu — last writer wins. Each caller uses its own freshly built index for its Search/Origin call, so the cache may not reflect what the first caller is actually using, and the second caller's build duplicates work that was just done; if storage changes between the two walks the two indexes can diverge. Add per-key locking (e.g., a sync.Map of *sync.Mutex keyed by NamespacedResource, or use sync.Map directly) so only one goroutine builds a given index and other callers wait for it to be cached.

findings.title: search.init watch goroutine is not bound to the server's lifecycle
findings.body: search.init sets `watchctx := context.Background()` and passes it to `s.storage.WatchWriteEvents(watchctx)`, then spawns a goroutine that processes events with this background context. This context is completely independent of the server's cancellable context (`s.ctx`, which server.Stop cancels via s.cancel). Calling server.Stop therefore does not stop the search watch goroutine; it only terminates once the SQL backend itself is torn down (b.cancel) and the poller's defer closes the events channel. Combined with the missing comma-ok on the channel receive (related finding above), the goroutine can panic during shutdown rather than exit cleanly. The watch should be tied to a context derived from s.ctx so server.Stop halts search indexing promptly, and the backend poller should respect that context for cancellation.

findings.title: Two independent database pollers run for WatchWriteEvents
findings.body: Both search.init (search.go ~line 203) and server.initWatcher call s.backend.WatchWriteEvents, and the SQL backend starts a separate poller goroutine for each call. Each poller runs `listLatestRVs` plus per-resource `poll` queries against the database every defaultPollingInterval (100ms), producing essentially the same event stream. With both watchers active the backend is doing two full sets of polls for what could be a single shared source. Before this PR these two watchers were also started, but lazily on the first gRPC call; after this PR they are both started eagerly and synchronously inside NewResourceServer, so this 2x DB load is now paid on every startup. Consider having a single backend.WatchWriteEvents source that fans out to the search index and the broadcaster (e.g., a shared channel that searchSupport.handleEvent and the broadcaster both subscribe to).

findings.title: Postgres branch is skipped instead of fixed in the integration test
findings.body: The new lines `// TODO - fix this test for postgres` plus `t.Skip(...)` for GRAFANA_TEST_DB == "postgres" hide a real test reliability problem rather than fixing it. Now that NewResourceServer blocks on Init during module server construction, this code path is more sensitive to slow or failing init, which is plausibly contributing to the CI failure (the comment says "Works locally" but not in Drone). A skip only papers over the failure: the postgres path is no longer exercised at all in CI, so future regressions on it will go unnoticed. The TODO should be tracked and the test should actually run for postgres in CI, or the broader problem should be diagnosed (e.g., separate slow init in NewResourceServer from module server startup so the test has a chance to complete).
